page: Amazon Web Services m4.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.4 GHz and includes a 45 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the m4.xlarge in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng and Geekbench tests, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall within the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including cached and uncached read/write operations, similarly rank in the bottom 25%, with uncached read speeds reaching 24.01 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations show lower relative efficiency, falling into the bottom 10% of benchmarked systems. Static web serving throughput is recorded at 3.36 GB/sec, and small-model LLM inference yields 71.79 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m4.xlarge represents an older hardware generation. While it offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, its resource density and processing throughput are lower than modern alternatives, making it a legacy option for workloads that do not require high-compute density. This instance is best utilized for low-intensity general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, small-scale development environments, and legacy applications that require dedicated CPU allocation without demanding high memory bandwidth or intensive parallel processing.
